steps.message:
# SceneActBench · Reconstruction

You are working in a Linux container with a **headless Blender** instance. Control it through the
**`blender` MCP tools** (most importantly `execute_blender_code`, `render_scene_view`,
`get_scene_info`, `get_object_info`). The Blender scene starts empty.

- **Reference images** are in `/app/input/` (`render_0000.png`, `render_0001.png`, `render_0002.png`, `render_0003.png`, `render_0004.png`, `render_0005.png`).
  Open and look at them; they are your only visual evidence.
- **Your answer is the 3D scene you leave in Blender.** When you finish, the furniture meshes in the
  Blender scene are exported and scored against a hidden 3D ground truth. As a safeguard, also save the
  scene before you stop, by running this with `execute_blender_code`:
  `import bpy; bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath='/app/output/scene.blend')`

The task instructions follow.

---

You are a procedural 3D modeling expert. Given multiple reference images of an
indoor scene (a room with a few pieces of furniture), you reconstruct EVERY furniture piece in
Blender by writing bpy code, matching its geometry AND its visible color.

# Input
- N reference images of the SAME room from different camera viewpoints (each with a known camera
  pose). Use them as multi-view evidence: cross-reference views to resolve depth, proportions,
  occluded structure, and hidden sides.
- The Blender scene starts EMPTY. The reference images are NOT available to your script at runtime.

# Reading the references — do this carefully BEFORE you build
1. Identify each furniture piece visible in any view. Count them.
2. For each piece, infer:
   - Category and characteristic shape.
   - Overall dimensions (length × width × height) in METERS, calibrated against the room.
   - Position and yaw (rotation about Z) in the world frame given the camera poses.
   - Symmetries (bilateral / radial), repeating sub-parts (slats, drawers, legs, lamp shades).
   - Distinctive ornament (panels, drawer pulls, mattress, pendant cords).
3. When images give clear quantitative cues (e.g. "4 legs", "3 drawers", "5 hanging cords"),
   reproduce those counts EXACTLY rather than approximating.
4. Read the dominant Base Color of every piece so each gets the right material color.

# Geometry quality bar
For each furniture piece, push for as much geometric detail as the reference shows. Compose
multiple primitives + bmesh edits + modifiers. Use bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_*_add for body shapes;
use bmesh operators (bevel / extrude / inset) to add edges and indents; use array / mirror
modifiers for repeating parts (legs, slats, drawers); exploit symmetry (mirror modifier) for
bilateral pieces. Do not ship a single naked cube for a complex piece.

Keep total mesh complexity under a few hundred thousand vertices. Build at real-world scale
(meters), every piece sitting on the floor (lowest Z = 0). World is Z-up.

# What NOT to build
- NO room shell: no floor plane, no walls, no ceiling, no skirting boards, no windows, even
  though the references show them. Furniture only.
- NO decorative props (books, plants, pictures) unless they are unmistakably present and large.
- DO NOT try to reproduce textures / patterns / fabric weave; only solid Base Color is required.

# Materials
For every mesh object, attach a Principled BSDF material with the correct Base Color, e.g.:
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new("m_bed_frame"); mat.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = next(n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED")
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (r, g, b, 1.0)
    obj.data.materials.append(mat)
Set roughness ≈ 0.7 and metallic = 0 by default (override only when clearly metal/glossy).

# How to place pieces
Set the FULL world matrix (T @ R) — rotation_euler/location piecemeal can fail under MCP:
    import bpy, mathutils
    obj = bpy.data.objects["bed"]
    T = mathutils.Matrix.Translation((x, y, z))
    R = mathutils.Matrix.Rotation(yaw_radians, 4, 'Z')
    obj.matrix_world = T @ R

# Workflow — iterate until satisfied
Build the scene with execute_blender_code, then call render_scene_view at one or more reference
camera poses. Compare each render to the corresponding reference image at the SAME camera angle,
walking through this priority list (in this order):

  1. MISSING PIECES — components in the reference that you did not build at all.
  2. WRONG SILHOUETTE / overall shape of an existing piece.
  3. WRONG PROPORTIONS / size — sizes or aspect ratios visibly disagree with the reference.
  4. WRONG COUNT of repeating parts — legs, drawers, lamp shades, hanging cords.
  5. MISALIGNMENT / FLOATING / wrong yaw.
  6. MISSING GEOMETRIC DETAIL — flat where the reference shows ribs / panels / drawer fronts /
     pleats / multiple lamp shades / etc.
  7. WRONG COLOR — Base Color visibly off vs the reference.

If any priority-1..6 item is clearly wrong, fix it with execute_blender_code, render again, and
re-evaluate. Stop when no priority-1..6 issue remains and priority-7 is at most "minor color
drift". You decide when it is good enough — you have a limited step budget, but use it.

# Conservatism bias
Each fix risks breaking working code. If a piece is recognizably correct and the only differences
are minor proportions or color, leave it alone. Do not rewrite working pieces every round.

When you stop, give a one-paragraph summary of what you built and any remaining differences from
the reference. Do NOT ask clarifying questions; if references are ambiguous, choose reasonable
defaults consistent with the visible views and the object category.

# Grading you'll be measured on
- Per-object f-score and Chamfer (geometry accuracy after global + local alignment).
- Per-object PointBERT cosine (3D semantic similarity — does it look like the right object).
- Per-object position error.
- Multi-view rendered visual fidelity (MSSIM / CLIP / LPIPS) against the references.
You get NO points for rooms, walls, or decorations; you get points for accurate furniture.

---

Reconstruct this indoor scene in 3D from 6 reference images of the SAME ROOM taken from different camera viewpoints (Blender starts empty).

World frame: Z-up, meters. fov_x = 39.6 deg.

Reference images and their camera poses (each in the same world frame):
  - view 0: /app/input/render_0000.png
      cam pos = [3.559, -6.1649, 2.5165], look_dir = [-0.4851, 0.8403, -0.2419], up = [-0.1209, 0.2095, 0.9703]
  - view 1: /app/input/render_0001.png
      cam pos = [9.3792, 0.0, 4.1553], look_dir = [-0.9397, 0.0, -0.342], up = [-0.342, 0.0, 0.9397]
  - view 2: /app/input/render_0002.png
      cam pos = [3.8437, 6.6581, 2.6585], look_dir = [-0.4851, -0.8403, -0.2419], up = [-0.1209, -0.2095, 0.9703]
  - view 3: /app/input/render_0003.png
      cam pos = [-3.7225, 6.4482, 3.4516], look_dir = [0.4698, -0.8138, -0.342], up = [0.171, -0.2962, 0.9397]
  - view 4: /app/input/render_0004.png
      cam pos = [-8.303, 0.0, 2.8118], look_dir = [0.9703, 0.0, -0.2419], up = [0.2419, -0.0, 0.9703]
  - view 5: /app/input/render_0005.png
      cam pos = [-5.0644, -8.7726, 4.4285], look_dir = [0.4698, 0.8138, -0.342], up = [0.171, 0.2962, 0.9397]

Treat the 6 images as MULTI-VIEW evidence of one room (not separate rooms). Cross-reference them to resolve depth, hidden sides, and exact furniture positions.

Step 1 — IDENTIFY every furniture piece visible in any view (bed, wardrobe, nightstand, pendant lamp, dresser, ...). Count them. Read the dominant Base Color of each piece.
Step 2 — For each piece, infer its real-world size (m), world position (x,y,z) and yaw (radians about Z), then plan the geometry: which primitives + bmesh edits + modifiers (mirror/array) you'll use to capture the silhouette and repeating parts.
Step 3 — BUILD with execute_blender_code: create geometry + materials, set obj.matrix_world = T @ R for placement.
Step 4 — RENDER each piece's appearance with render_scene_view at the SAME camera poses listed above; compare to the reference views by priority (missing pieces > silhouette > proportions > count of repeating parts > misalignment > detail > color); fix and re-render until the room matches.
  Also create EXTRA cameras at other angles (e.g. a top-down view and a side view) and render_scene_view from them — the reference poses are 2D projections, so depth errors and objects floating / sunk into the floor only show from other angles. Verify the 3D layout, not just the reference silhouette.
Step 5 — Stop when satisfied; do not ask questions.

REMINDERS:
  - Furniture only. NO floor / walls / ceiling / windows / decorations.
  - Real-world meters; lowest Z = 0; do NOT rescale objects after placement.
  - Reproduce exact counts (legs, drawers, hanging cords) when visible.
  - Use bmesh / mirror / array modifiers for detail and repeating parts; do not ship naked cubes for complex pieces.
I'll start by examining the reference images to identify the furniture pieces.

import bpy, sys, numpy as np, os
# usage: blender --background --python crop.py -- <in.png> <out.png> x0 y0 x1 y1 scale
argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--")+1:]
src, dst = argv[0], argv[1]
x0,y0,x1,y1,s = [int(v) for v in argv[2:7]]
img = bpy.data.images.load(src)
w,h = img.size
px = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h,w,4)
px = px[::-1]  # top-down
crop = px[y0:y1, x0:x1]
crop = np.kron(crop, np.ones((s,s,1), dtype=np.float32))
ch, cw = crop.shape[:2]
out = bpy.data.images.new("out", cw, ch, alpha=True)
out.pixels = crop[::-1].ravel().tolist()
out.filepath_raw = dst
out.file_format = 'PNG'
out.save()
print("saved", dst, cw, ch)

import bpy, sys, numpy as np

# Load all 6 views, print color-class pixel bboxes
classes = {
    'pink':   lambda r,g,b: (r>170)&(r<235)&(g>120)&(g<185)&(b>120)&(b<190)&(abs(g-b)<40)&(r-g>25),
    'dark':   lambda r,g,b: (r<90)&(g<90)&(b<90)&(abs(r-g)<25)&(abs(g-b)<25),
    'wood':   lambda r,g,b: (r>130)&(r<225)&(g>85)&(g<180)&(b>40)&(b<140)&(r-g>25)&(g-b>15),
    'gray':   lambda r,g,b: (abs(r-g)<12)&(abs(g-b)<12)&(r>100)&(r<175),
    'khaki':  lambda r,g,b: (r>150)&(r<215)&(g>130)&(g<200)&(b>70)&(b<160)&(r-b>40)&(g-b>25)&(r-g<45),
    'lggray': lambda r,g,b: (abs(r-g)<12)&(abs(g-b)<12)&(r>=175)&(r<245),
    'white':  lambda r,g,b: (r>=235)&(g>=235)&(b>=235),
}

for i in range(6):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(f'/app/input/render_000{i}.png')
    w,h = img.size
    px = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h,w,4)[::-1]
    r,g,b = px[...,0]*255, px[...,1]*255, px[...,2]*255
    print(f'=== view {i} ===')
    for name, fn in classes.items():
        m = fn(r,g,b)
        # ignore background: white bg pixels are (255,255,255) but antialiased edges included
        ys,xs = np.nonzero(m)
        if len(xs) < 50:
            print(f'  {name}: none'); continue
        print(f'  {name}: n={len(xs)} x[{xs.min()},{xs.max()}] y[{ys.min()},{ys.max()}]')
        # print row bands (contiguous y ranges with many pixels) to separate stacked objects
        colcount = m.sum(axis=1)
        rows = np.nonzero(colcount > 8)[0]
        if len(rows):
            bands=[]; s=rows[0]; p=rows[0]
            for rr in rows[1:]:
                if rr-p>4: bands.append((s,p)); s=rr
                p=rr
            bands.append((s,p))
            print(f'    ybands: {bands}')

import bpy, sys, numpy as np

classes = {
    'pink':   lambda r,g,b: (r>170)&(r<235)&(g>120)&(g<185)&(b>120)&(b<190)&(abs(g-b)<40)&(r-g>25),
    'dark':   lambda r,g,b: (r<90)&(g<90)&(b<90)&(abs(r-g)<25)&(abs(g-b)<25),
    'wood':   lambda r,g,b: (r>130)&(r<225)&(g>85)&(g<180)&(b>40)&(b<140)&(r-g>25)&(g-b>15),
    'gray':   lambda r,g,b: (abs(r-g)<12)&(abs(g-b)<12)&(r>100)&(r<175),
    'khaki':  lambda r,g,b: (r>150)&(r<215)&(g>130)&(g<200)&(b>70)&(b<160)&(r-b>40)&(g-b>25)&(r-g<45),
    'lggray': lambda r,g,b: (abs(r-g)<12)&(abs(g-b)<12)&(r>=175)&(r<245),
}

def label(m):
    h,w = m.shape
    lab = np.zeros((h,w), dtype=np.int32)
    cur = 0
    from collections import deque
    for sy in range(h):
        xs = np.nonzero(m[sy] & (lab[sy]==0))[0]
        for sx in xs:
            if lab[sy,sx]: continue
            cur += 1
            q = deque([(sy,sx)]); lab[sy,sx]=cur
            while q:
                y,x = q.popleft()
                for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny,nx = y+dy,x+dx
                    if 0<=ny<h and 0<=nx<w and m[ny,nx] and lab[ny,nx]==0:
                        lab[ny,nx]=cur; q.append((ny,nx))
    return lab, cur

for i in range(6):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(f'/app/input/render_000{i}.png')
    w,h = img.size
    px = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h,w,4)[::-1]
    r,g,b = px[...,0]*255, px[...,1]*255, px[...,2]*255
    print(f'=== view {i} ===')
    for name, fn in classes.items():
        m = fn(r,g,b)
        if m.sum() < 100: continue
        lab, n = label(m)
        if n == 0: continue
        counts = np.bincount(lab.ravel())[1:]
        for c in np.argsort(counts)[::-1][:8]:
            area = counts[c]
            if area < 150: break
            ys,xs = np.nonzero(lab==c+1)
            print(f'  {name}#{c+1}: area={area} x[{xs.min()},{xs.max()}] y[{ys.min()},{ys.max()}]')

def add_cam(name, pos, look, up):
    look = Vector(look).normalized(); up = Vector(up).normalized()

import bpy, math
from mathutils import Vector, Matrix

# ---------------- helpers ----------------
def purge():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete()
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.cameras, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.images):
        for b in list(block):
            if b.users == 0:
                try: block.remove(b)
                except Exception: pass

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    """dims=(sx,sy,sz) full sizes; center in piece-local coords."""
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0), major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def bool_cut(target, cutter):
    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    mod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):
    mod = obj.modifiers.new("bev", 'BEVEL')
    mod.width = width; mod.segments = segments
    mod.angle_limit = math.radians(angle)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts:
        p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

def place(obj, x, y, yaw=0.0):
    T = Matrix.Translation((x, y, 0.0))
    R = Matrix.Rotation(yaw, 4, 'Z')
    obj.matrix_world = T @ R

# ---------------- materials ----------------
m_pink    = mat("m_pink",    (0.78, 0.57, 0.57))
m_char    = mat("m_char",    (0.16, 0.16, 0.17))
m_white   = mat("m_white",   (0.82, 0.82, 0.83))
m_gray    = mat("m_gray",    (0.47, 0.47, 0.49))
m_knob    = mat("m_knob",    (0.78, 0.78, 0.78))
m_tvback  = mat("m_tvback",  (0.72, 0.72, 0.73), rough=0.5)
m_screen  = mat("m_screen",  (0.06, 0.06, 0.07), rough=0.3)
m_khaki   = mat("m_khaki",   (0.45, 0.40, 0.26))
m_wood    = mat("m_wood",    (0.67, 0.52, 0.36))
m_tbrown  = mat("m_tbrown",  (0.55, 0.35, 0.19))
m_ttop    = mat("m_ttop",    (0.76, 0.72, 0.65), rough=0.4)
m_pole    = mat("m_pole",    (0.72, 0.63, 0.42))
m_shade   = mat("m_shade",   (0.64, 0.60, 0.71), rough=0.8)
m_rim     = mat("m_rim",     (0.50, 0.47, 0.58))
m_silver  = mat("m_silver",  (0.80, 0.80, 0.82), rough=0.3, metal=0.9)
m_darkkn  = mat("m_darkkn",  (0.10, 0.10, 0.11))

parts = []   # temp holder for current piece

# ================= 1. TV media console =================
P = []
P.append(box("c_base", (0.42, 1.81, 0.10), (0, 0, 0.05), m_pink))
P.append(box("c_top",  (0.42, 1.81, 0.15), (0, 0, 0.475), m_pink))
P.append(box("c_back", (0.12, 1.81, 0.30), (-0.15, 0, 0.25), m_pink))
post_ys = [-0.875, -0.52875, -0.17625, 0.17625, 0.52875, 0.875]
for i, py in enumerate(post_ys):
    P.append(box(f"c_post{i}", (0.30, 0.0725 if 0 < i < 5 else 0.06, 0.30), (-0.0? if False else 0.06, py, 0.25), m_pink))

import bpy, math
from mathutils import Vector, Matrix

# ---------------- helpers ----------------
def purge():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete()
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.cameras, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.images):
        for b in list(block):
            if b.users == 0:
                try: block.remove(b)
                except Exception: pass

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),
                                     major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def bool_cut(target, cutter):
    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    mod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):
    mod = obj.modifiers.new("bev", 'BEVEL')
    mod.width = width; mod.segments = segments
    mod.angle_limit = math.radians(angle)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts:
        p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

def place(obj, x, y, yaw=0.0):
    T = Matrix.Translation((x, y, 0.0))
    R = Matrix.Rotation(yaw, 4, 'Z')
    obj.matrix_world = T @ R

# ---------------- materials ----------------
m_pink    = mat("m_pink",    (0.78, 0.57, 0.57))
m_char    = mat("m_char",    (0.16, 0.16, 0.17))
m_white   = mat("m_white",   (0.82, 0.82, 0.83))
m_gray    = mat("m_gray",    (0.47, 0.47, 0.49))
m_knob    = mat("m_knob",    (0.78, 0.78, 0.78))

m_silver  = mat("m_silver",  (0.80, 0.80, 0.82), rough=0.3, metal=0.9)
m_darkkn  = mat("m_darkkn",  (0.10, 0.10, 0.11))

# ================= 1. TV media console (cubbies on +X face) =================

P.append(box("c_top",  (0.42, 1.81, 0.15), (0, 0, 0.475), m_pink))

post_ys = [-0.875, -0.52875, -0.17625, 0.17625, 0.52875, 0.875]
for i, py in enumerate(post_ys):
    w = 0.06 if i in (0, 5) else 0.0725
    P.append(box(f"c_post{i}", (0.30, w, 0.30), (0.06, py, 0.25), m_pink))
# 2 small knobs on each long face
for s in (-1, 1):

        P.append(cyl(f"c_knob", 0.014, 0.02, (dx, s * 0.915, 0.28), m_darkkn,
                     rot=Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(90), 4, 'X')))
console = join_parts(P, "console")
place(console, 1.66, 0.14)

# ================= 2. TV on console (screen faces -X) =================
P = []
P.append(box("tv_foot", (0.18, 0.50, 0.035), (0, 0, 0.5675), m_khaki))
P.append(box("tv_neck", (0.05, 0.07, 0.25), (0, 0, 0.71), m_khaki))
panel = box("tv_panel", (0.06, 1.60, 0.85), (0, 0, 1.105), m_tvback)
bevel(panel, 0.025, 3, 60)
P.append(panel)
cut = box("tv_cut", (0.04, 0.95, 0.55), (0.03, 0, 1.02), None)
bool_cut(panel, cut)   # recess on back (+X) face
P.append(box("tv_screen", (0.006, 1.56, 0.81), (-0.033, 0, 1.105), m_screen))
tv = join_parts(P, "tv")
place(tv, 1.66, 0.14)

# ================= 3. Gray 6-drawer cabinet (drawers face +X) =================
P = []
P.append(box("g_leg1", (0.14, 0.25, 0.18), (0, -0.21, 0.09), m_white))
P.append(box("g_leg2", (0.14, 0.25, 0.18), (0, 0.21, 0.09), m_white))
body = box("g_body", (0.42, 0.80, 0.65), (0, 0, 0.505), m_gray)
P.append(body)
P.append(box("g_cap", (0.44, 0.82, 0.02), (0, 0, 0.84), m_gray))
rows = [0.3025, 0.5075, 0.7125]
cols = [-0.185, 0.185]
k = 0
for rz in rows:
    for cy in cols:
        P.append(box(f"g_fr{k}", (0.015, 0.35, 0.185), (0.2175, cy, rz), m_gray))
        P.append(cyl(f"g_kn{k}", 0.016, 0.025, (0.235, cy, rz), m_knob,
                     rot=Matrix.Rotation(math.radians(90), 4, 'Y')))
        k += 1
cabinet = join_parts(P, "cabinet")
place(cabinet, -1.55, 0.0)

# ================= 4. Dark open cubby unit 4x5 (openings face +/-X) =================
P = []
for sx in (-1, 1):
    for sy in (-1, 1):
        P.append(box(f"u_leg", (0.07, 0.07, 0.23), (sx * 0.12, sy * 0.65, 0.115), m_white))
P.append(box("u_bot", (0.35, 1.50, 0.035), (0, 0, 0.2475), m_char))
P.append(box("u_top", (0.35, 1.50, 0.035), (0, 0, 1.0625), m_char))
for sy in (-1, 1):
    P.append(box("u_end", (0.35, 0.035, 0.85), (0, sy * 0.7325, 0.655), m_char))
for dy in (-0.3675, 0.0, 0.3675):
    P.append(box("u_div", (0.30, 0.035, 0.78), (0, dy, 0.655), m_char))
for sz in (0.412, 0.574, 0.736, 0.898):
    P.append(box("u_shelf", (0.30, 1.43, 0.03), (0, 0, sz), m_char))
unit = join_parts(P, "cubby_unit")
place(unit, 1.60, -1.65)

# ================= 5. Slab B (above unit) & 6. Slab A (wall shelf) =================
sb = box("slab_b", (0.40, 1.50, 0.08), (0, 0, 1.24), m_char)
place(sb, 1.95, -1.60)
sa = box("slab_a", (0.35, 1.50, 0.06), (0, 0, 1.98), m_char)
place(sa, 1.70, -1.58)

P.append(cyl("l_foot", 0.085, 0.10, (0, 0, 0.05), m_pole, r2=0.028))

import bpy, numpy as np, sys

def load(path):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(path)
    w, h = img.size
    a = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    a = a[::-1]  # top-down
    rgb = a[..., :3]
    bpy.data.images.remove(img)
    return rgb

def classify(rgb):
    r, g, b = rgb[...,0], rgb[...,1], rgb[...,2]
    mx = rgb.max(-1); mn = rgb.min(-1)
    sat = mx - mn
    v = mx
    classes = np.zeros(rgb.shape[:2], dtype=np.int32)
    # 1 pink, 2 dark(charcoal/screen), 3 wood, 4 gray-light, 5 khaki, 6 pale
    classes[(r > 0.6) & (g > 0.35) & (g < 0.75) & (b > 0.35) & (b < 0.75) & (r - g > 0.08) & (r - b > 0.08) & (abs(g-b) < 0.1)] = 1
    classes[(v < 0.38) & (sat < 0.12)] = 2
    classes[(r > 0.4) & (r - b > 0.12) & (g - b > 0.05) & (r > g) & (g > b)] = 3
    classes[(sat < 0.12) & (v >= 0.38) & (v < 0.75)] = 4
    classes[(r - b > 0.08) & (r - b < 0.35) & (g - b > 0.03) & (v > 0.35) & (v < 0.8) & (g > r * 0.75)] = 5
    classes[(sat < 0.2) & (v >= 0.75)] = 6
    return classes

def comps(mask, min_px=60):
    # simple BFS connected components
    h, w = mask.shape
    seen = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=bool)
    out = []
    idxs = np.argwhere(mask)
    maskb = mask.astype(bool)
    for y, x in idxs:
        if seen[y, x]:
            continue
        stack = [(y, x)]
        seen[y, x] = True
        ys, xs = [y], [x]
        while stack:
            cy, cx = stack.pop()
            for dy, dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                ny, nx = cy+dy, cx+dx
                if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and maskb[ny, nx] and not seen[ny, nx]:
                    seen[ny, nx] = True
                    stack.append((ny, nx))
                    ys.append(ny); xs.append(nx)
        if len(ys) >= min_px:
            out.append((min(xs), max(xs), min(ys), max(ys), len(ys)))
    return sorted(out, key=lambda t: -t[4])[:8]

NAMES = {1:'pink',2:'dark',3:'wood',4:'gray',5:'khaki',6:'pale'}
for path in sys.argv[-2:]:
    rgb = load(path)
    cls = classify(rgb)
    print('====', path)
    for c in range(1, 7):
        m = cls == c
        if m.sum() < 60:
            continue
        print(f'-- {NAMES[c]} ({m.sum()}px)')
        for x0, x1, y0, y1, n in comps(m):
            print(f'   x {x0}-{x1} (c{(x0+x1)//2})  y {y0}-{y1} (c{(y0+y1)//2})  n={n}')

import bpy, numpy as np, sys

def load(path):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(path)
    w, h = img.size
    a = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)[::-1]

import bpy, numpy as np

def load(path):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(path)
    w, h = img.size
    a = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)[::-1]
    rgb = a[..., :3]
    bpy.data.images.remove(img)
    return rgb

def med(path, x0, y0, x1, y1):
    rgb = load(path)
    # my renders are 800px; scale coords
    s = rgb.shape[0] / 768.0
    reg = rgb[int(y0*s):int(y1*s), int(x0*s):int(x1*s)].reshape(-1, 3)
    m = np.median(reg, axis=0)
    return (m[0], m[1], m[2])

# my render regions (768-coord space, auto-scaled)
MY = [
    ('my_1.png', 350,395,480,455, 'tv_back'),
    ('my_1.png', 300,485,510,545, 'console'),
    ('my_1.png', 70,405,250,500, 'unit'),
    ('my_1.png', 600,380,670,470, 'dresser'),
    ('my_1.png', 540,385,600,420, 'shade'),
    ('my_1.png', 550,430,575,530, 'pole'),
    ('my_1.png', 350,330,430,360, 'cabinet'),
    ('my_3.png', 300,400,420,450, 'tabletop'),
    ('my_5.png', 350,385,450,430, 'tabletop5'),
    ('my_5.png', 490,330,540,420, 'slabA'),
]
for path, x0, y0, x1, y1, label in MY:
    m = med(path, x0, y0, x1, y1)
    print(f'my {label:10s}: ({m[0]:.2f}, {m[1]:.2f}, {m[2]:.2f})')
# table top tighter samples from refs
for path, x0, y0, x1, y1, label in [

]:
    m = med(path, x0, y0, x1, y1)
    print(f'{label:12s}: ({m[0]:.2f}, {m[1]:.2f}, {m[2]:.2f})')

steps.message: Key findings: console cubbies are open-through with tall openings, unit has overhanging top slab, lamp shade sits lower. Let me resolve the slab_b question in v0:
steps.reasoning_content:
EXCELLENT detail! Now I can see:

**CONSOLE (q_r_v1con)**: 
- Pink body, sits directly on floor ✓
- 5 cubby openings on +X face ✓, openings are TALL RECTANGLES (not arched — square tops), spanning nearly full body height: openings from just below top slab to near bottom. Opening height ≈ 60% of body; top slab thick (~15% of height); bottom rail thin.
- The openings show WHITE background through them at the top!! Look: inside each opening, upper part shows WHITE (light) and lower part darker pink-ish — the openings are OPEN-THROUGH! (white bg visible through upper portion). Actually looking carefully: each cubby interior: upper region white/light, lower region shaded pink — this is an open-through compartment with the far side open, white bg beyond, and the interior bottom visible. YES — the console cubbies are OPEN THROUGH (like the unit!). Hmm — wait, but v4 said console back is plain?? Let me recheck: in v4 (from −x) the console showed as plain gray?? The v4 gray comp x 316-449 y 435-561 — maybe that was something else. If console cubbies are open-through, from v4 we'd see white/pink striped face... Hmm, v4 ref: I need to look. Actually wait — in v4 the TV (x 1.57-1.75) stands directly BEHIND the console's +X openings plane?? The console x 1.45-1.87, openings on +X face (x 1.87 plane), through-depth to x 1.45. From v4 (−x side), looking at console back (x 1.45 face): the openings would show as openings in the BACK face too (through) — but the TV (x 1.57-1.75, dark screen facing −x) sits immediately behind, filling the view through the cubbies! So from v4, the console back would show... the openings would reveal the TV's dark screen → the back face would read as pink frame + dark openings — but measured v4 gray comp 316-449 y 435-561 (0.44 gray)... hmm that comp is BIG (13680px). If the console back had dark openings, the dark class would show. v4 dark comps: 272-461 y 260-362 (TV) — that's ABOVE (y 260-362), the console region y 435-561 has no dark. So from v4 the console back shows NO dark openings?! 

Hmm wait — actually from v4 the console is BEHIND the coffee table?? no, table at y −0.47..0.77, console y −0.89..1.19 — they overlap in y! From v4 (looking +x): the table (x −0.45..0.25) is CLOSER to cam than console (x 1.45). The table (0.45 tall, top z 0.45) partially occludes the console's lower part!! The v4 gray comp 316-449 y 435-561 = console back visible ABOVE the table?? and below hidden... The table top z 0.45; console cubbies z 0.10-0.50: the cubby region is mostly BEHIND the table from v4! Only the top slab band (z 0.50-0.62) + sliver visible. So the v4 "plain" reading was inconclusive — the cubbies were hidden behind the table!! GREAT — so console cubbies ARE open-through (per v1 white bg) and v4 is consistent (occluded).

Hmm wait, actually — let me re-examine: in q_r_v1con, the white in the cubbies: could it be the white CONSOLE INTERIOR back panel (lit) rather than background? The white region in each cubby is at the TOP of the cubby, and the cubby interior bottom is pink-dark. If the back were closed and painted white inside, the whole interior back would be white-ish uniformly... The pattern (white top, shaded bottom) matches SEEING THROUGH to the bright sky/white bg at the top of the opening (since we look DOWN 20°, through the opening we see: the interior floor (bottom, pink, shadowed) and above it the far opening → white bg). ✓ OPEN-THROUGH confirmed.

So console: open-through cubbies, 5 compartments, tall openings. Opening geometry from crop: body height 0.62: top slab ~0.12, bottom rail ~0.06, openings z ≈ 0.06..0.50 (0.44 tall). Widths: 5 openings, dividers thin (~0.04): opening w = (2.08 − 6*0.04 − 2*0.05)/5 ≈ 0.35?? From crop: opening width ≈ 0.30-0.33, dividers ~0.05. Let me set: opening w 0.32, gap 0.055: total = 5*0.32+4*0.055+2*0.075 = 1.6+0.22+0.15 = 1.97 ≈ 2.08 ✓ adjust.

Also console TOP: the TV pedestal foot sits on top ✓ khaki foot visible ✓.

Also console top surface: pink ✓. The knobs: NOT visible in v1 on +X face ✓ (as decided).

**UNIT (q_r_v1unit)**: 
- 4 cols × 5 rows grid ✓✓ CONFIRMED (4 columns, 5 rows of open-through cubbies, white bg visible through ✓).
- The unit has a THICK TOP SLAB that OVERHANGS! Look: the top slab is wider than the body (overhangs on all sides, esp. front-left) and there's a shadow gap below it — the top slab is a separate thicker panel ~like slab_b!! Interesting — so the "slab_b" I built floating above might actually be... no wait — the crop shows the unit: top overhanging slab + body with 4×5 grid + legs. The overhanging top slab IS part of the unit (z ~1.08-1.20?) — and "slab_b" at 1.23-1.31 is ANOTHER slab above?? In this crop I see only ONE top slab (overhanging). Hmm — where's slab_b in this view? slab_b at y −2.35..−0.85, unit y −2.5..−1.0: slab_b is ABOVE the unit from this angle → would appear just above the unit top... The crop top shows the overhang slab. Maybe the overhang IS slab_b (touching the unit top)! I.e., the unit body top ~1.08 and slab_b (1.5×0.4×0.08) sits directly ON the unit top as an overhanging top panel!! That resolves the v0 confusion (dark region continuity, no gap!). But ref v3 seemed to show a GAP between slab and unit... Let me check ref v3 unit region again... earlier full v3 view: the unit at (280-370, 240-370) with a slab above (255-370, 225-255) — there appeared to be separation. Hmm — but at v3's angle a slab sitting ON the unit (overhanging toward +x) could still show a shadow line. 

Actually look at the v1 unit crop again: the top slab clearly OVERHANGS to the LEFT (−y side... in v1 left = +y?? v1 right = +y: the slab overhangs on the LEFT = −y side... hmm the image shows overhang on left and right edges). The slab bottom edge has a dark shadow line on the body below it. If slab_b sat ON the unit (bottom z = unit top 1.08), from 20° above we'd see: slab top surface, slab front edge, and the unit's top surface strip behind... but here the body top is NOT visible (slab covers it + overhangs). ✓ consistent with slab sitting on top.

BUT the v0 view: slab_b overhang toward +X (x 1.75-2.15 vs unit 1.43-1.77): from v0 (cam at +x,−y), an overhang toward +x would be prominent... In ref v0 p_r_unit crop: the slab appears well ABOVE the unit's grid with a white gap?! Hmm — in p_r_unit (ref v0 crop 380-630/350-480): the dark slab band at top, then WHITE gap, then the unit below with grid starting. The white gap between slab and unit... that gap is the white BACKGROUND visible between the slab (z 1.2-1.28) and the unit top (z 1.08)?? A 0.12 gap at that distance would be thin (~10px)... the crop showed a substantial white region. UNLESS in v0 the unit's TOP is set BACK (the slab overhangs +x beyond the unit top's front edge, so between the slab's front-bottom edge and the unit's front-top edge, you see through to white bg ABOVE the unit top — because the unit top surface at 14° camera elevation: you'd see the top surface, not white... hmm, if the slab overhangs PAST the unit's front face, looking from above-front, under the overhang you'd see shadow/underside, not white.

ALTERNATIVE: slab_b is genuinely FLOATING above the unit with a real gap (~0.15-0.25), AND the unit has its own thin overhanging top slab. From v1 crop: I see the overhang slab directly on the body (no white gap — the shadow line is tight). If there were a floating slab 0.2 above, at 20° elevation it would appear clearly separated with white bg between (from v1 the bg behind is white) — NOT observed. So in v1: slab ON unit. In v0: white gap observed?! Both can't hold unless the "gap" in v0 is actually the shadow/underside... 

Let me re-crop ref v0 unit/slab region larger to resolve definitively.

**LAMP (q_r_v1lamp)**:
- Shade: lilac/lavender, TRUNCATED CONE, with PLEATED texture (vertical ribs visible as zigzag pattern!) and a TOP OPENING showing interior (darker inside) with a rim — the shade top is OPEN (we see into it). There's a thin khaki/yellow rim wire at the top opening edge ✓.
- Pole: khaki, TAPERED (wider at bottom), with a TRUMPET FOOT at the base (flares out at bottom) ✓ my build has trumpet foot ✓.
- Shade proportions: bottom width ~100px (crop 3x → 33px at 768 → 0.26m?? hmm: crop region 510-610 (100px wide at 768) scaled 3x = 300px. Shade spans crop x ~85-265 → 60px at 768 → 0.47m bottom diameter ✓ matches r 0.25. Shade height: crop y 75-165 → 30px at 768 → 0.28m ✓.
- Shade bottom z: pole visible from foot to shade: shade bottom at crop y ~165 → px_y 415 (768): for lamp (1.51,1.45): z: r = (384−415)/1067 = −0.029: 0.9397z−1.209 = −0.029*(8.816−0.342z) → 0.9397z−1.209 = −0.2557+0.0099z → 0.9298z = 0.9533 → z = 1.025. Shade bottom z ≈ 1.03, top ≈ 1.31. Total lamp: pole to 1.03, shade 1.03-1.31. Pole floor to 1.03 = 1.03 tall. OK — so lamp total ~1.31. My build: shade 1.17-1.45 (too high by 0.14), pole to 1.17. FIX: pole 0..1.02, shade z 1.02..1.30.

Hmm interesting — the v1-based shade z (0.96-1.29 earlier) ✓ consistent ~1.03-1.31. v0-based was 0.76-1.04 — I distrust v0 reading (pale comp contamination). Go with 1.02-1.30.

Now re-crop ref v0 unit region to settle slab_b.

steps.reasoning_content:
NOW it's clear!

**v0 slab region**: slab_b is a WIDE SLAB whose top face is visible (light gray, we see it from above at 14°... wait we see a LOT of top face). The slab extends from lower-left to upper-right diagonally. Below/right of it: the unit with 4×5 grid. The slab's LEFT portion hangs over WHITE background (no unit below it at the left end!) — the slab is LONGER than the unit's projected width or offset. And importantly, the slab appears SEPARATED from the unit top by a shadow... hmm, actually looking at the v0 crop: the slab's dark front edge runs diagonally; below it directly is the unit's top region (dark). At the left end, below the slab: white bg then the pale tabletop... So slab_b: at its left (−y) end, there's nothing below (white bg) — the unit (y −2.5..−1.0) vs slab (y −2.35..−0.85): they overlap... From v0, the slab's LEFT end in image = the −y end?? screen right = +0.866x+0.5y → for the slab (fixed x), the +y end is right. Left end = −y end (y −2.35). Below the slab's −y end: white bg — but the unit spans y −2.5..−1.0, so below the slab's −y end (y −2.35) there SHOULD be unit (unit extends to −2.5)... unless the unit is NOT below that part — unit x 1.43-1.77 vs slab x 1.55-1.95: the slab overhangs +x by 0.18; from v0 (cam +x side), the slab's overhang hides... hmm, actually what's below the slab's left end in the image could be the unit's TOP surface — but it shows WHITE. 

WAIT — look at v4 crop instead — MUCH clearer:
**v4 unit region**: TOP: slab_a (long thin dark slab, edge-on with slight top face visible) at y_px 190-215. MIDDLE: slab_b (another long dark slab, slightly thicker, top face visible) at y_px 295-325. BOTTOM: the unit (4×5 grid, open-through with WHITE bg through openings ✓✓) with legs, top at y_px ~345. AND CRUCIAL: there's a BIG WHITE GAP between slab_b (bottom ~325) and the unit top (~345)!! In v4 (from −x, looking +x at 14° down): if slab_b sat ON the unit, no gap. The white gap = background between slab_b bottom (z 1.28?) and unit top... The gap ~20px: vertical px scale at unit distance (z_cam ~9.6 from −x cam... unit x 1.6: vx = 9.9, z_cam ≈ 9.9*0.9703 + ... ≈ 10.0): px_per_m = 1112/10 = 111 (800px). 20px gap → 0.18m gap. Hmm but wait — in v4, could the "gap" be the unit's top surface?? The unit top surface would be DARK (charcoal) not white. The gap is WHITE → real space. So slab_b FLOATS ~0.15-0.2 above the unit top. But then v1's crop showed the slab ON the unit... In q_r_v1unit the top overhang slab — maybe THAT is the unit's own overhanging top (z 1.08-1.20), and slab_b floats above it at 1.28-1.38?? From v1 at 20° elevation looking at the unit face-on: a floating slab 0.15 above the unit top would show a white gap... the v1 crop shows the overhang slab tight on the body. UNLESS the floating slab_b is EXACTLY behind/above aligned such that from v1 it hides behind the overhang slab's projection?? From v1 (looking −x from above 20°): slab_b at z 1.28-1.36, x 1.55-1.95; unit top slab at z 1.08-1.20, x 1.43-1.77(+overhang). Projection: slab_b (higher AND further +x = closer to v1 cam... wait v1 cam at x 9.379 — larger x = closer). slab_b x up to 1.95, its top z 1.36: projected px_y: for (1.75,−1.75,1.36): vx = −7.629, vz = −2.795: z_cam = 7.169+0.956 = 8.125; y_cam = 2.609−2.626 = −0.017 → px_y = 384+2 = 386. Unit overhang top (z 1.20) at (1.6,−1.75): vx = −7.779, vz = −2.955: z_cam = 7.310+1.011 = 8.321; y_cam = 2.660−2.777 = −0.117 → px_y = 384+15 = 399. So slab_b at 386, unit top slab at 399 — 13px apart — with the slab_b depth (x extent 0.4 → projected height ~0.4*sin20°... the slab_b's own projected vertical extent: from its near-bottom edge to far-top edge ≈ (0.4*0.342 + 0.08)*1067/8.1 ≈ 24px. So slab_b occupies px_y ~380-404; unit top slab occupies ~395-410 → THEY OVERLAP in projection from v1!! The white gap (0.15m vertical) projects to ~... the gap between slab_b bottom (1.28) and unit top (1.20) at slab x... projects to a few px — HIDDEN behind the slabs themselves. ✓✓ CONSISTENT with v1 showing them merged!

And in v4 (from −x): slab_b x 1.55-1.95 vs unit 1.43-1.77: slab_b is FURTHER from v4 cam → appears HIGHER (smaller depression angle) + the gap 0.15 projects: gap in px: between slab_b bottom edge (at x 1.55, z 1.28) and unit top (at x 1.77, z 1.20): px_y slab_b bottom: v = (1.55+8.303, −1.75, 1.28−2.81) = (9.853,−1.75,−1.53): z_cam = 9.560+0.370 = 9.930; y_cam = 2.386−1.484 = 0.902 → px_y = 400−101 = 299 (800). unit top (1.77,−1.75,1.20): v = (10.073,−1.75,−1.61): z_cam = 9.773+0.389 = 10.162; y_cam = 2.438−1.513 = 0.925 → px_y = 400−101 = 299?!? Hmm wait, I mis-set the geometry: from v4 (−x side), the unit's top FRONT edge (x 1.43, the near face) is what bounds the unit silhouette top... and slab_b bottom edge at its NEAR end (x 1.95!! — slab_b extends to 1.95, CLOSER to v4 cam than the unit near face 1.43!). Recompute: slab_b near-bottom edge (1.95,−1.75,1.28): v = (10.253,−1.75,−1.53): z_cam = 9.948+0.370 = 10.318; y_cam = 2.481−1.484 = 0.997 → px_y = 400−107 = 293. So UNIT: body top 1.20, legs 0.23, body 0.23..1.20 (0.97 tall). Grid: 4 cols × 5 rows THROUGH-openings with white visible ✓. import bpy, numpy as np

def load(path):
    img = bpy.data.images.load(path)
    w, h = img.size
    a = np.array(img.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)[::-1]
    rgb = a[..., :3]
    bpy.data.images.remove(img)
    return rgb

rgb5 = load('input/render_0005.png')
rgb3 = load('input/render_0003.png')
rgb0 = load('input/render_0000.png')

print('ref v5 table region rows (x 340-460):')
for y in range(375, 450, 10):
    row = []
    for x in range(340, 465, 20):
        p = np.median(rgb5[y:y+6, x:x+6].reshape(-1,3), axis=0)
        row.append(f'({p[0]:.2f},{p[1]:.2f},{p[2]:.2f})')
    print(f'y{y}: ' + ' '.join(row))
print('ref v3 table region rows (x 280-450):')
for y in range(395, 480, 10):
    row = []
    for x in range(280, 455, 25):
        p = np.median(rgb3[y:y+6, x:x+6].reshape(-1,3), axis=0)
        row.append(f'({p[0]:.2f},{p[1]:.2f},{p[2]:.2f})')
    print(f'y{y}: ' + ' '.join(row))
print('ref v0 table region rows (x 300-480):')
for y in range(390, 470, 10):
    row = []
    for x in range(300, 485, 25):
        p = np.median(rgb0[y:y+6, x:x+6].reshape(-1,3), axis=0)
        row.append(f'({p[0]:.2f},{p[1]:.2f},{p[2]:.2f})')
    print(f'y{y}: ' + ' '.join(row))

def purge():

    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),

    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))

from mathutils import Vector, Matrix

# ---------------- helpers ----------------
def purge():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete()
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.cameras, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.images):

            if b.users == 0:
                try: block.remove(b)
                except Exception: pass

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),
                                     major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def bool_cut(target, cutter):
    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    mod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):
    mod = obj.modifiers.new("bev", 'BEVEL')
    mod.width = width; mod.segments = segments
    mod.angle_limit = math.radians(angle)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts:
        p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

    T = Matrix.Translation((x, y, 0.0))
    R = Matrix.Rotation(yaw, 4, 'Z')
    obj.matrix_world = T @ R

        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),
                                     major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):
    mod = obj.modifiers.new("bev", 'BEVEL')
    mod.width = width; mod.segments = segments
    mod.angle_limit = math.radians(angle)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj

]
def frame(c,l,u):
    L=np.array(l,float); U=np.array(u,float); L/=np.linalg.norm(L); U/=np.linalg.norm(U)

    return np.array(c,float),L,R,U
def woodmask(a):

import bpy, numpy as np
from collections import deque
cams = [
 ((3.559,-6.1649,2.5165),(-0.4851,0.8403,-0.2419),(-0.1209,0.2095,0.9703)),

 ((-5.0644,-8.7726,4.4285),(0.4698,0.8138,-0.342),(0.171,0.2962,0.9397)),
]
def load(p):
    img=bpy.data.images.load(p); w,h=img.size
    a=np.array(img.pixels[:],dtype=np.float32).reshape(h,w,4)[:,:,:3][::-1]
    bpy.data.images.remove(img); return (a*255).astype(int)
def woodmask(a):
    r,g,b=a[:,:,0],a[:,:,1],a[:,:,2]
    return (r>90)&(r<215)&(r>g+12)&(g>=b)&(b>30)
def frame(c,l,u):
    L=np.array(l,float); U=np.array(u,float); L/=np.linalg.norm(L); U/=np.linalg.norm(U)
    R=np.cross(L,U); R/=np.linalg.norm(R); return np.array(c,float),L,R,U
def components(m,minsize=400):
    h,w=m.shape; seen=np.zeros_like(m,bool); out=[]
    for y in range(0,h,4):
        for x in range(0,w,4):
            if m[y,x] and not seen[y,x]:
                q=deque([(y,x)]); seen[y,x]=True; pts=[]
                while q:
                    cy,cx=q.popleft(); pts.append((cy,cx))
                    for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        ny,nx=cy+dy,cx+dx
                        if 0<=ny<h and 0<=nx<w and m[ny,nx] and not seen[ny,nx]:
                            seen[ny,nx]=True; q.append((ny,nx))
                if len(pts)>=minsize:
                    ys=[p[0] for p in pts]; xs=[p[1] for p in pts]
                    out.append((min(xs),max(xs),min(ys),max(ys),len(pts)))
    return out
def proj(px,py,C,L,R,U,zplane):
    xc=(px-384)/1067.0; yc=(384-py)/1067.0
    d=L+xc*R+yc*U
    t=(zplane-C[2])/d[2]
    P=C+t*d
    return P[0],P[1]
for i in range(6):
    a=load(f"/app/input/render_000{i}.png"); m=woodmask(a)
    comps=components(m)
    C,L,R,U=frame(*cams[i])
    print(f"--- view {i}")
    for (x0,x1,y0,y1,n) in comps:
        # project 4 corners to z=0.3 and z=1.0 planes
        p=[]
        for zp in (0.3,1.0):
            p.append([proj(x0,y0,C,L,R,U,zp),proj(x1,y1,C,L,R,U,zp)])
        print(f"  comp n={n} px {x0}-{x1} y {y0}-{y1}")
        print(f"    z0.3: TL({p[0][0][0]:.2f},{p[0][0][1]:.2f}) TR({p[0][1][0]:.2f},{p[0][1][1]:.2f})")
        print(f"    z1.0: BL({p[1][0][0]:.2f},{p[1][0][1]:.2f}) BR({p[1][1][0]:.2f},{p[1][1][1]:.2f})")
EOF

def purge():

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),
                                     major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def bool_cut(target, cutter):
    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    mod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):
    mod = obj.modifiers.new("bev", 'BEVEL')
    mod.width = width; mod.segments = segments
    mod.angle_limit = math.radians(angle)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts:
        p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),

    o = bpy.context.active_object
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')

def purge():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete()

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),
                                     major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    mod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):
    mod = obj.modifiers.new("bev", 'BEVEL')
    mod.width = width; mod.segments = segments
    mod.angle_limit = math.radians(angle)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts:
        p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

# ---------------- helpers ----------------
def purge():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete()
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.cameras, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.images):

                try: block.remove(b)
                except Exception: pass

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),
                                     major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def bool_cut(target, cutter):
    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    mod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):
    mod = obj.modifiers.new("bev", 'BEVEL')
    mod.width = width; mod.segments = segments
    mod.angle_limit = math.radians(angle)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)

def join_parts(parts, name):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
    for p in parts:
        p.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = parts[0]
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.name = name
    return obj

from mathutils import Vector, Matrix

# ---------------- helpers ----------------
def purge():
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.object.delete()
    for block in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.cameras, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.images):
        for b in list(block):
            if b.users == 0:
                try: block.remove(b)
                except Exception: pass

def mat(name, color, rough=0.7, metal=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name)
    if m is None:
        m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def _finish(o, name, center, material):
    o.name = name
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Translation(center))
    if material is not None:
        o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def box(name, dims, center, material, rot=None):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0, 0, 0))
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    o.data.transform(Matrix.Diagonal((*dims, 1.0)))
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def cyl(name, r, depth, center, material, r2=None, rot=None, verts=24):
    if r2 is None:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    else:
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(radius1=r, radius2=r2, depth=depth, location=(0,0,0), vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    if rot is not None:
        o.data.transform(rot)
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def torus(name, R, r, center, material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(major_radius=R, minor_radius=r, location=(0,0,0),
                                     major_segments=32, minor_segments=12)
    o = bpy.context.active_object
    return _finish(o, name, center, material)

def bool_cut(target, cutter):
    mod = target.modifiers.new("cut", 'BOOLEAN')
    mod.operation = 'DIFFERENCE'
    mod.object = cutter
    mod.solver = 'EXACT'
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = target
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    bpy.data.objects.remove(cutter)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=2, angle=50):

**Done — scene saved to `/app/output/scene.blend`.**

**Summary of what I built.** The scene contains 9 furniture meshes at real-world scale (all resting at Z=0, meters, Z-up), reconstructed from the 6 multi-view references: (1) a pink open console/TV-bench at (1.66, 0.16) — top slab, bottom rail, dividers forming 5 through-openings, black end caps and knobs; (2) a TV on it with pale-gray panel, recessed back, dark screen, and khaki foot+neck protruding forward; (3) a gray 6-drawer cabinet (2×3, round knobs, white block legs) at (−1.90, 0.04) with drawers facing +X; (4) a charcoal near-black 4×5 cubby unit with overhanging top cap and white legs at (1.60, −1.75), plus two floating charcoal shelves (slab_b above the cubby at z≈1.3, slab_a wall shelf at z≈2.0); (5) a floor lamp at (1.51, 1.45) with tapered khaki pole, trumpet foot, pleated lavender shade and rim torus; (6) a coffee table at (−0.10, 0.15) with brown wood body, four through-openings on the long aprons, tapered round legs and a wood top (pale from the v0/v4 viewing angles via gloss, brown in v2/v5 as in the refs); and (7) a 12-drawer dresser (3 cols × 4 rows with silver bar handles, pale top cap, small legs) at (0.02, 2.45) with yaw 0 — a key late finding was that the drawer fronts and handles are visible on **both** long faces (south in views 0/1/4/5, north in views 2/3), so it was built double-sided. Every piece has a Principled BSDF with base colors calibrated numerically against the reference pixels (wood ≈ (152,124,100) rendered, charcoal cubby ≈ (55,55,55), console pink matched exactly). Remaining known deviations are minor: ±0.1 m residual ambiguity in the dresser's exact footprint/height across views (view-consistent fits disagree by ~10–15 px), the coffee-table top reads brown in my v4 render where the reference shows a paler sheen, and wood-grain texture is not reproduced (solid base colors only, per instructions).
